claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game has an online-only requirement and lacks an offline mode.

citations.review_text:
Always have been a good game with a good potential. Now it's even better, but unfortunately still online only. I hope they will port a good part of Payday 2 into PD3 and create more heists and do QOL so most of us can finally move on to Payday 3.
(Originally played on GamePass)

I really wanted PAYDAY 3 to succeed.

The gameplay itself isn't the problem. Gunplay feels good, stealth is a genuine improvement over PAYDAY 2 in many ways, and the visuals are exactly what you'd expect from a modern sequel.

The problem is that everything around that foundation feels smaller.

There are fewer heists, fewer weapons, less customization, simpler skill builds, less replayability, and far fewer reasons to keep playing. After completing each heist in loud and stealth a few times, it already feels like you've experienced almost everything the game has to offer.

Playing solo doesn't help either. The AI teammates are unreliable, often getting stuck, ignoring objectives, or standing around while you're doing all the work. Combined with the always-online requirement, even solo play can end because of connection issues, which is frustrating for no good reason.

Progression also feels unrewarding. PAYDAY 2 constantly gave you something to work toward, whether it was new builds, Infamy, achievements, or simply experimenting with different playstyles. PAYDAY 3 never gives that same feeling. It hands you most things too quickly, and once you've reached the endgame, there isn't much incentive to stay.

What disappoints me most isn't that PAYDAY 3 is a terrible game.

It's that it doesn't feel like a sequel to PAYDAY 2.

The shooting is better. The stealth is better. The graphics are better.

Almost everything else feels like a downgrade.

I don't hate PAYDAY 3.

As a longtime fan of the series, I expected more...

Review: A promising game covered in diarrhea.
(I played the game by “sailing the seas” method for 3 years. I finally bought this just to write this review, and I bought it at full price out of pity, not because it earned it.)

Good Side:
=========

This game genuinely feels like an upgrade from my beloved Payday 2. The graphics, guns, animations, and sounds all just click, and I love that part of it. Base heists are somewhat fun, and the AI pathfinding and difficulty scaling have improved a lot compared to the last game. The stealth system feels more readable and less janky in some situations, and when it works, it actually feels smoother than PD2. I also like the vendor system, it gives a proper underworld black market vibe. Skills are fairly balanced and not completely broken like some PD2 builds used to be. Gunplay overall feels heavier and more grounded, and the hit feedback is genuinely satisfying when the game isn’t busy tripping over itself.

Bad Side:
========

Oh boy, there’s a lot of shjt to unpack here. First and biggest issue is the complete lack of offline mode. Payday has always been a co-op shooter, but requiring a live server was never a necessity. Starbreeze forced this online-only crap down everyone’s throat. People begged for offline mode, got promises, waited years, and then got hit with “not feasible.” That’s not just a middle finger to your core player base, it’s a self-inflicted death sentence for preservation and long-term playability.

Offline Mode Rant:

Dear Starbreeze, we know exactly why you did this. Your fanbase is not stupid or naive. This entirely contrived online-only BS exists so you can gatekeep progression, check DLC ownership, and keep your little store ecosystem running. All to prevent people from saving a few dollars in the most ineffective way possible.

But let’s be honest, did it work? No. Your servers are barely more secure than a school computer lab. People have been playing this game and its DLCs for free anyway (includi…

After everything I heard about this game, I wanted to give it a fair chance. After waiting this long for it to pull it's ♥♥♥♥ together, I was hopeful I was in for a good experience. Dear god, was I wrong.

Firstly, the game is pretty smooth and high-quality... when I get to play it. Graphically it's quite good. The combat system helps make up for weak-feeling weaponry and I enjoyed playing the one heist I actually got to play.

Now let's talk about everything WRONG here:

The overall stability and functionality of the game is utterly disastrous! I could, for the most part, connect to a game just fine, but when it came to actually joining the game, I would sometimes crash to desktop, get stuck in spectator mode with NO WAY to leave without having to close the game and the one time I did manage to join a game in progress, I had to stand around like an idiot for like 30 seconds while my character put their mask on, and the heist was pretty much already done anyway.

2 years... and this is how much they've patched the game? Are you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ serious, Starbreeze!?

As someone who's been a dedicated Payday fan since the very first game when UberHax0rNova played it, I'd hoped at the bottom-line very least it was playable. But most of my time here was either staring at a loading screen or watching as other people played the game.

This is unacceptable.

Do not buy this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game locks missions and prevents returning to the lobby if players get caught while entering the garage after stealthing First World Bank.

citations.review_text: From the cringe corny lines to the bull charging dozers, this game is a huge downgrade in many ways. The soundtrack is just not as good too and what led me to write this review was the fact that I perfectly stealthed First World Bank just to get caught while entering the garage. Ended up hard locking the mission as I was told to go back to the lobby but with the door locked, I could not find a way back to the bank.

For what this game is, it's really great. Especially for this price.

But they gotta revamp the tutorial to be more action packed or something. I bought this game and was iffy through out the tutorial. My brother and boyfriend both refused to play the game until I hooked them up with family sharing to even try the game out. I wasn't even sure I liked the game, and refunded it before deciding to try one more time.

Then, the cocaine car shop (Search and Seizure) happened, and I was hooked. I desperately beg you to play Search and Seizure as your first main heist, because it's what got me hooked, If you play either bank heist, you're just gonna think it's run-of-the-mill bank robberies. But this mission and the Road Rage mission really, REALLY sold me on it.

Search and Seizure is about tearing apart cocaine mule cars and stealing the cocaine that's inside. Is there anything more Payday than that, mission-wise? You do an odd thing to get a lot of money. In loud it's action packed, great for learning, and proof that it's more than boring bank robberies.

So, let's go over the enemies real quick, a grand majority if not all of them got major tweaks, and there's even new faces. And every one has a great personality that's been enhanced tenfold. On top of that, they can ALL appear on Normal, and definitely get buffed on higher difficulties.

First, the Tazer is now called the Zapper. Not totally thrilled with the name change or the new model, but their gameplay has changed a bit. It takes them longer to tase you, and now carry a taser pack on their side. If you shoot the taser pack, all people (civvies, players, cops etc) around him are tased, including himself. It's quite funny to see.

Second, we have shields. Besides their actual shield looking more imposing, they look pretty normal, like in 2. Shields went from dorky little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you'd pop through their metal in two seconds to actual danger. Their shields aren't easily pierced, and unless you can get around them or …

claims.claim: Reviewers report that stealth gadgets have extremely limited uses and cannot be picked back up after placement.

citations.review_text:
This feedback comes from someone who never played the famous Payday 2, but has spent a lot of time playing stealth-focused games like Hitman and Shadow Tactics, which I absolutely love.

1. Raid rather than Stealth

One thing I really enjoy about Payday 3 is that it takes a step further by having crazy puzzle mechanics i havent seen in any other games ive played before. Planning a route, manipulating guards, and solving the map feels very satisfying.

However, I feel like the game leans much more toward raid gameplay than stealth gameplay. The tools intended to support a stealth approach often feel too limited or too weak, especially on larger maps.

2. Tools

Most stealth gadgets have an extremely limited number of uses. Yes, I know there are skills that improve them, but even with those they still feel underpowered.

For example, why can't we pick gadgets back up after we're done using them? 

If you've already cleared one section of the map, those gadgets become useless once you reach another area. This becomes especially noticeable on the larger heists, which I actually enjoy because they offer more room for planning and playground.

Take the Motion Sensor as an example. I place it, use it to deal with maybe two guards, and then it's gone forever—even though there might still be twenty guards patrolling the rest of the map. 

On top of that, its detection radius feels tiny. Three meters feels incredibly small for a gadget that's so limited in uses. Is the only purpose to stick it on someones back? I was hoping it also works on walls and such.

3. Searching Phase

I honestly don't understand why the Search Phase is infinite.

If guards become suspicious, they should search the area for a while, but eventually conclude that nothing is there and return to normal patrols.

Right now, once you trigger a search, you're basically forced into one of two choices:

- start eliminating everyone or restart the entire heist. Its just frustrating.

Since the game already allo…

I played a lot of payday 2 back in the day and based on my experiences in both games i can say that Payday 3 does some things better and some things worse, its a mixed bag.
Stealth is definetly better, the possibility of doing a whole heist unmasked is amazing. 
The public/restricted areas make for a great "noob safety net" that dont automatically fail your hard earned sneaking around shenenigans and hacking skills make things more manageable.
Even if you fail stealth, you still have some form of usefulness in loud as you have slots for both silent and loud gameplay so even if you messed up at the end you can still make it work.
The only stinking thing here is lackluster planning.
Favors are one time use only and good luck earning them, its a rng drop after finishing any heist + you can buy some of them in a shop in the main menu of the game before the heist, PD2 did it better and i hope the devs can work on that.
As for loud, its fun, guns feel great and mowing down hordes of cops is as fun as ever. AI of the normal cops has improved, they advance in groups, hide behind their shield holding colleagues and overall feel good to fight against.
As for specials, they are alright.
Dozers feel like a big threat comapred to PD2, cloakers got some fancy moves wallruning, sliding or jumpscaring you from above, techies and granadiers feel like a good addition to the roster.
The only weak side of specials are tasers and snipers. Tasers dont tase much and snipers dont have their audio cues from PD2.

Overall, PD3 in its current state is an ok game. Sure, some things are missing and the content is not that much at the moment but i hope the devs will get it there to the PD2 level and above.

Get it on sale and see for yourself, im not disappointed.

im an avid payday 2 fan... and i came in being skeptical if i would enjoy the more tactical and stealthy gameplay of payday 3 because i was used to such chaos in payday 2, yet it is a very nice change of pace. and as of late the stealth mechanics are very well made, tho sometimes unrealistic... it is much better then payday 2 stealth. but many people talk about the stealth of payday 3, i want to say that loud in payday 3 is also very enjoyable, the chaos is still there... maybe not as prominent as payday 2, but it can get messy sometimes. but the thing i enjoyed most about payday 3's loud is how the difficulty comes in waves, in payday 2 if you go on a deathwish loud heist... it'll be hard from the second you start to the second you end, but if you take on an overkill loud heist in payday 3 you get the difficulty in waves, maybe its easier in hallways where you can mow down cops, but may be harder in more open areas. and that variability is refreshing. 

payday 3 does have its cons, the amount of heists is considerably small. but every heist is very well thought out and well made. the range of weapons is small, and the amount of modifications you can make to guns is also limited. and there sometimes are crashes and freezes, and some bugs or glitches that may prove annoying 

in general, if you love the payday franchise and also are open to trying out stealth mechanics or have already played and enjoyed games with those mechanics (such as hitman, or other stealth focused games) then payday 3 is an amazing option, just try not to buy it full price... wait for a discount for the best bang for your buck

I played Payday 2 on PS3, PS4 and PC for probably a combined amount of 1000 hours. I just started to play Payday 3 after I got it during a Sale with all its DLC and I must say: It's really good. Sure it lacks Content if you compare it to Payday 2 but PD 2 is 13 years old. Thats 10 years older than PD3. 

I really like the Gunplay, Graphics and Performance of it. Also it has Crossplay (huge Win). It feels like a modernized Payday 2. I really hope the Devs will continue the Good Update Cycles and keep pushing out new Content. Because that is the biggest downside in my Opinion. We need more Heists, more Guns, Perkdecks and more End-Game Challenges. I don't care if we get another Remake of Slaughterhouse or Heat Street. I just need more playable Heists and Guns

Let me start by saying that I love Payday 2 and that I only started playing Payday 3 this year. The current state of the game feels like a worthy successor to Payday 2. It feels similar but upgraded in many ways. The only thing I can think of where it is worse than Payday 2, is in the content department. We could use a bit more heists, heisters and weapon options.

It's a good game and I hope people who hated it at launch give it another shot.
game is great, just lacks content and the level of customization/cosmetics payday 2 has. stealth and overall gunplay is way better in 3. def worth trying, especially if they keep adding content

its good
not as much content as payday 2 but its not payday 2 so whatever, still a fun, good game but we need more content that ARENT dlcs

Payday 3 isn't a terrible game. It introduces some genuinely good ideas and improves parts of the formula, but it often feels like it was developed by a team that didn't fully understand what made Payday so memorable.
Comparing Payday 3 to a game with over 10 years of updates isn't, by itself, why it has so many negative reviews. The lack of content is not the only part of the problem. In my opinion, the biggest issue is that Payday 3 lost much of the identity that made the franchise stand out.

[h1]What Payday 3 Got Right[/h1]

[h2]Maskless Stealth[/h2]
Being able to complete parts of a heist without putting on your mask is an excellent addition. You can now perform actions like picking up keycards, hacking phones, cameras, or computers while still blending in. It allows you to push stealth much further before , making heists feel more "strategic".

[h2]Remote Camera Hacking[/h2]
Another welcome improvement is the ability to hack cameras remotely. In Payday 2 you had find the security room to access the entire system. In Payday 3, hacking a single camera gives you access to all of them, removing unnecessary busywork..

[h2]Moving Cameras[/h2]
Security cameras are no longer fixed in place. They now rotate and cover different areas, creating more opportunities to move through blind spots if you're patient enough.

[h2]More Natural Guards[/h2]
One of the biggest frustrations with Payday 2 stealth was how guards seemed to have eyes in the back of their heads. In Payday 3, they behave much more naturally, detecting you only when they actually have line of sight. This makes stealth significantly less frustrating.

[h2]Public, Private and Secure Areas[/h2]
The new area system works perfectly with maskless stealth. Entering a secure area usually results in a guard escorting you out instead of immediately failing the stealth. Truly private areas remain dangerous, where being spotted has real consequences. This makes mistakes less punishing while still rewarding careful play…

Improved and better than the poor launch and still improving now. It's fun but with it's issues and not bad for on sale.
I'd still recommend Payday 2 over 3 if not owned already. 
As an Assault only player, I'm very happy to see "Stealth Only" heists to have Loud options now, something they should always have. 
Even the stealth is more fun here despite how short I do it before going loud. You can even beat heists without ever putting on your masks and it's definitely better than 2's.

citations.review_text:
Credit where credit is due because Payday 3 has had such a turnaround from when it released. 

It brings all the adrenaline and edge of your seat action of Payday 2 with [b]EXTREMELY satisfying gunplay[/b]. It looks beautiful, it runs well, it's polished, the difficulty is rewarding, the music is brilliant, stealth is miles above PD2 in terms of complexity. And the talents and level reworks they've been doing have hit the sweet spot. 

It feels unfair to compare the amount of content in this to its predecessor, when 2 has a solid 10 years worth of releases over Payday 3. 

For a game that's been out nearly 3 years and had a rocky start, it's in a good place right now.

Sure it lacks Content if you compare it to Payday 2 but PD 2 is 13 years old. Thats 10 years older than PD3. 

I really like the Gunplay, Graphics and Performance of it. Also it has Crossplay (huge Win). It feels like a modernized Payday 2. I really hope the Devs will continue the Good Update Cycles and keep pushing out new Content. Because that is the biggest downside in my Opinion. We need more Heists, more Guns, Perkdecks and more End-Game Challenges. I don't care if we get another Remake of Slaughterhouse or Heat Street. I just need more playable Heists and Guns

A weak imitation, and a complete waste of potential, because of greed and incompetence.
Overall: Not worth it. 

The positives: The Gunplay is a great improvement to the previous games, and a welcome one, The graphics are ok? Nothing crazy. The hostage system is improved and feels realistic but arcady enough. The stealth is massively improved and viable.

The negatives: The music is a downgrade from the previous games. The game was half-baked or mismanaged, and launched that way. Many things have been changed to be like the previous game, which is lazy and was a waste of time. You also need to make an account for the game? What a hassle. The new replacement for Bain is obnoxious, terribly writen and is just a ESG brownie point. Many unnecessary woke elemants. Uses an unoptimized game engine (Unreal 5). The weapon, character, skill progression system is DOG POOP. No real sense of prestige or end goal. The money you get is werid and most of it is useless. 

This game is basically two games: Updated Payday 3 and launch Payday 3. Launch was disgusting, fixing things that worked, taking things out, shallow, member-berries reliant, DLC shenanigans, woke, and is just a worse product than launch Payday 2. Payday 3 updated? Just Payday 2 but better gameplay, but with mediocre dlc, annoying female bain, mandatory account, no real end game or even safe house, the lore is tame.

As a long term fan of Payday 2 when it came out: Do not buy.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that DLC packs contain missions and weapons, but some express that the DLCs are overpriced.

citations.review_text:
PAYDAY 3 – A Good Foundation with Plenty of Potential

PAYDAY 3 is a fun co-op game that can provide a lot of entertainment, especially when playing with friends. The heists are well designed and give you the freedom to approach them in different ways, whether you prefer stealth or going in loud. The gameplay feels smooth, and unlocking new weapons and equipment gives you a reason to keep playing.

Unfortunately, the base game doesn't offer enough heists, so they start to feel repetitive after a while. The DLCs with new missions and weapons bring some fresh content and make the game fun again for a while, but that feeling doesn't last very long. Once you unlock better gear, the enemies also stop being much of a challenge, even on the highest difficulty.

It's also disappointing that the developers don't seem to focus more on expanding the game with meaningful content. Instead of adding more heists or interesting gameplay features, many of the newer DLCs are mostly cosmetic items like character outfits, which don't really add much to the overall experience. The game has a lot of potential, but I feel like it's not being fully utilized.

Despite these issues, PAYDAY 3 is still an enjoyable co-op game, especially with friends. I just hope the developers continue to support it with more worthwhile content in the future because the core gameplay is genuinely fun.

My Rating: 6.5/10.

do i think this game should have happened? yes, I will not take back my excitement for the announcement of payday 3. 

the armor system is interesting, and i like how much potential it adds to every build.

gunplay? ehhhhh if im being honest, sometimes it feels a little strange. once you get the weapon level up, then its pretty good, but outside of that the weapons sometimes feel like peashooters.

this game is fun, but not so much with randoms or solo. 6/10

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game has significantly less content and fewer heists available compared to Payday 2.

citations.review_text:
I did like the game when it came out, even if I had to accept, that it had multiple glaring issues.

The support for the game in the first two years post launch was also horrendously bad.
But for the entire year of 2026 so far (writing comment on 27.07.26) there have been regular well done updates.

The crew supporting the game was massively upgraded in terms of numbers and the game is now actually good IMO. They have already updated some of the "old" heists that had some lame/annoying mechanics and replaced them with better ones, as well as adding areas or changing the starting position and layout of other heists.

With the current quality and quantity of updates, I firmly believe this game has the chance to actually become great if this keeps up. 
I've recently been playing a lot and having tons of fun with it.

There is still less content for this game than for payday2, but I just enjoy the gameplay so much more.

The stealth, movement are so much better than payday2. This one actually feels really smooth to heist in stealth, where I always felt payday2 was lacking and actually really clunky.

IMO the game is definitely worth what you pay for it, especially if you can get it on a sale.

in a vacuum this game is pretty good! great gunplay, fun build crafting and. some of the spectacles really engage that heisting fantasy. But you cant talk about it without mentioning the disastrous launch, incredibly weird monetization choices, tones down heist count compared to payday 2 and the fact that most of the new updates don't add anything new. while i'm kinda bashing this game i do think its worth its fairly low pricetag (depending on your region) and it would make for a few weeks of good fun with friends. But tbh i would still recommend payday 2 more.
